audit.why: 53.34% over 808 games. The chart gives Yasuo levels 3-5 and both item stages and Camille levels 1 and 6, which reads harsh against a 53% lane — but the prose explains the gap the same way the Volibear entry does: Camille's win comes from converting the level-6 window and closing the game, not from winning the stat check. Consistent and defensible.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is written as Camille's trump card with no mention of what Yasuo gains at 6, and Last Breath is only ever 'his R'.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 and falls to 30s at rank 3 — one of the shortest ultimates in the game. The text does note that it goes off any team knockup in the late-game section, but at level 6 itself it says only 'look to all-in or roam every time it's up' about Camille's ultimate. Against a 30s-at-rank-3 ultimate the asymmetry the reader should understand is that Camille gets one arena per 140s while Yasuo gets a reset every 30s off anyone's crowd control — including, in a skirmish, off Camille's own Hookshot knockup.
audit.corrected: Last Breath named with its 70s-to-30s range, and the interaction that Hookshot's landing knockup is itself a Last Breath trigger stated in mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's defect is right: no Yasuo ability is named. The text uses 'his Q poke', 'his E-dashes', 'flow shield', 'Windwall' and 'his R' throughout. Camille's R appears without its article.
audit.why: Riot's kit is Way of the Wanderer (P) — the flow bar and the shield it grants — Steel Tempest (Q), Wind Wall (W), Sweeping Blade (E) and Last Breath (R). Two cooldowns carry the lane and neither appears: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 and only reaches 17s at rank 5, which is why spending it is a real cost to him; and Sweeping Blade is 0.5s at rank 1 down to 0.1s, which is why 'his E-dashes can't carry him out of the arena' is a meaningful claim rather than an obvious one — outside the arena that dash is functionally always available. Steel Tempest is 4s.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named; Wind Wall's 25s and Sweeping Blade's near-zero cooldown written in so the reader understands which of his tools is scarce and which is not.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Trade back only after your burst is on cooldown' and 'don't dump cooldowns into a Yasuo who's looking to flow-cancel' give the reader no timer on either side.
audit.why: Wind Wall at 25s is the only long cooldown Yasuo has in lane, so it is the only one worth tracking; everything else is back within seconds. Naming that turns a vague warning into the one thing to count.

The matchup's central insight — that Wind Wall is irrelevant to Camille's own engage and is therefore a tool he spends on her team's ranged CC rather than on her — is stated clearly in four places and is the kind of specific, decision-changing fact the rest of this champion's data lacks. See notes: I could not fully verify one component of it and have left it untouched rather than restate it.

edits.before: This is your lane to take over. Levels 4-5 you own short trades — bait his throwaway auto onto your passive shield, then E-Q-W bursts him before his flow regenerates a shield. At 6 your R is the trump card: Hextech Ultimatum is a leap, not a castable projectile, so Windwall can't stop it, and once he's inside the arena his E-dashes and flow mobility mean nothing — look to all-in or roam every time it's up. The only real respect line is his Q knockup setting up R for a quick burst back, so don't dump cooldowns into a Yasuo who's looking to flow-cancel and re-engage.
edits.after: This is your lane to take over. Levels 4-5 you own short trades — make him spend the 25s Wind Wall, then E-Q-W bursts him before Way of the Wanderer regenerates the shield. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum is the trump card: a leap, not a castable projectile, so Wind Wall can't stop it, and once he is inside the arena Sweeping Blade and his flow mobility mean nothing — all-in or roam every time it is up. The real respect line is Last Breath, 70s at rank 1 but only 30s by rank 3: it fires off any knockup, including your own Hookshot landing, so don't hand him a free reset in a skirmish.

notes: UNVERIFIED AND IMPORTANT — the matchup asserts four times that 'none of your kit is a projectile, so Wind Wall does nothing'. Camille's kit file carries a derived projectile flag on Hookshot, which directly contradicts that claim, while Riot's own description of Hookshot ('pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing') mentions no projectile at all. I could not resolve this from the kits and did not restate the claim in either direction — every edit above leaves the projectile sentences intact and only fixes names and cooldowns around them. Given that the calibration examples specifically call out a missed Wind Wall interaction, this one should be settled before the next pass; see questionsForUser. Separately, the packet defect 'never names any of Yasuo's abilities' is now cleared, and Last Breath was added at level 6 — it fires off any knockup including Camille's own Hookshot landing, which the matchup never mentioned.
